state.instructions: Evaluate whether the stated child-state change retains the specified delivery boundary.
state.facts: Booking notification and reminder guards already depend on its version. Mutating phase/revision on that booking from an asynchronous sales listener would change the version after the original service event. The replacement keeps initial charge source, allowance-adjusted monetary_due, site, resource product, purchased time and attribution scalars frozen on the booking, but records sales progress in a single CommercialSale child unique by parent. Owner-atomic lookup/create/update changes the child alone, and a phase change emits SaleMilestone keyed by Booking.source with that original amount. Under DESIGN an untouched parent retains its version when its child changes. Publish paid for positive money only with paid fulfillment, confirmed/occupied/completed service, consumed or unnecessary allowance, no cancellation/refund instructions and collected/refunded evidence; actual checked_out is necessary for completion. Cancellation, no_show and refunds fence reversal forever. Review or expiry reverses only previously published sales, leaving original unpaid late recovery intact. Invoice owns receipt validation and first-customer history proof. A ReservationChanged bridge queues CommercialCheck, while invalidation handlers send that check directly without repeating customer correspondence. Hour/day capture must belong to the same verified actor and booker/customer and match latest_capture(customer,actor,location,product). Quote handoff supplies the same four frozen origin scalars with its declared product, which Rent compares to resource.kind. Ordinary internal reservations can be unattributed. A refund deadline cannot justify cancellation_passed. This is a proposed contract with no executed runtime.
state.actual_code:
A created row has version 1 throughout its creating transaction, including create-hook adjustments. Ordinary references to an existing row expose its admitted version `v` throughout the owner transaction while field reads observe ordered provisional changes. An accepted `set`, CRUD update or archive reserves `v+1`, even for a normalized same-value write. Further writes/calls/hooks to that row do not advance it again. Update-hook `event.before.version` is `v` and `event.after.version` is the reserved `v+1`; create-after is 1. Permanent removal has no after record; its deleted event carries `v+1`. A child write does not advance an unwritten parent. Failed operations advance nothing; receipt replay reapplies nothing. This write-intent rule intentionally produces history/version changes for accepted no-op writes. Locks compare stored values, not modification metadata.
